name: user_creation_groups
description: A member's own list of creation groups. The entry with the lowest sort_order is their main one and pre-fills the group field on submission.

columns.name: sort_order
columns.description: Lowest wins. Ties are not resolved by the schema — see the note.

indexes.name: idx_ucg_user_id
indexes.note: Redundant with the leading column of uniq_user_creation_group. Do not recreate it in gradido2.

notes: The list is user-maintained AND moderator-editable: fixing a misspelled tag happens here, not on one contribution. Both writers use the same rows, so neither may assume it is the only one.

sort_order carries no unique constraint, so two rows can share the lowest value. Legacy breaks the tie by ordering sort_order ASC, id ASC — the row's own id, not the creation group's — and both implementations must use that same order, or a member sees a different main tag depending on which backend answered. Legacy assigns the values densely (a new row takes the current count), so a gap or a duplicate is a repair case rather than a state.
No foreign keys in legacy; see the open question in contribution_creation_groups.json.
